title: Service Discovery
subtitle: Dynamic endpoint registration, health-checked resolution, and client-side vs server-side vs service mesh discovery.
keyTakeaways: In containerized cloud environments, IP addresses are ephemeral: pods auto-scale, crash, and reschedule with dynamic network addresses.
A Service Registry (Kubernetes DNS, Consul, Eureka) acts as the single source of truth for active, healthy service instances.
Modern architectures favor Service Meshes (Envoy/Istio): sidecar proxies handle discovery, mutual TLS, and load balancing transparently without application code SDKs.
architectureDiagram:
CLIENT-SIDE VS SERVER-SIDE VS SERVICE MESH DISCOVERY
1. SERVER-SIDE (Kubernetes CoreDNS / Cloud Load Balancer):
   [ Client Pod ] ---> Resolves "order-service" via DNS ---> [ ClusterIP / LB ] ---> [ Pod A / B ]

2. SERVICE MESH (Sidecar Envoy Proxy - Modern Standard):
   [ Client Pod ] ---> Localhost:8080 ---> [ Local Envoy Sidecar ]
                                                    |
                                          Discovers & mTLS via Envoy Mesh
                                                    v
                                          [ Remote Envoy Sidecar ] ---> [ Server Pod ]

sections.heading: Service Registry and Ephemeral Infrastructure
sections.body: In traditional static server deployments, services called downstream dependencies via fixed IP addresses or stable DNS hostnames configured in properties files. In cloud-native container platforms (Kubernetes, AWS ECS), pods spin up, scale out, and terminate continuously. Hardcoded IPs break immediately. Service Discovery provides dynamic endpoint mapping.
bullets: Self-Registration: Instances register their dynamic IP and port with the Service Registry upon startup and deregister upon shutdown.
Continuous Health Check Heartbeats: The registry polls instances or listens for periodic heartbeats. If a pod crashes or fails health checks, it is stripped from active routing tables within seconds.
DNS Resolution (CoreDNS): In Kubernetes, every Service receives a virtual stable IP (ClusterIP) mapped to an internal DNS name (`order-service.default.svc.cluster.local`).

sections.heading: Client-Side vs Server-Side vs Service Mesh Discovery
sections.body: How clients route to discovered instances divides into three architectural patterns.
bullets: Server-Side Discovery (AWS ALB / K8s ClusterIP): The client calls a centralized load balancer or virtual IP; the load balancer queries the registry and routes traffic. Simplest client code; downside is an extra network proxy hop.

Client-Side Discovery (Netflix Eureka / Ribbon): The client queries the service registry directly, caches healthy instance IPs locally, and executes its own load balancing. Eliminates intermediate proxy hops; downside is language-specific client library lock-in.

Service Mesh Discovery (Envoy / Istio): Transparent sidecar proxies run alongside each container. The application simply calls `http://payment-service:8080`. The local Envoy sidecar intercepts the call, discovers healthy endpoints, enforces mTLS, and load balances transparently.

tradeOffs.pros: Decouples discovery, mTLS, retries, and tracing from application code; works identically across all programming languages.
tradeOffs.cons: Consumes memory for sidecar containers; adds ~1-2ms latency overhead per hop; complex control plane management.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Large polyglot microservice fleets in enterprise Kubernetes environments.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero third-party sidecar overhead; built directly into Kubernetes networking; straightforward operational model.
tradeOffs.cons: DNS caching in Java runtimes can cause stale IP lookups; lacks advanced canary routing and client-side circuit breaking.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Standard Kubernetes microservices without complex zero-trust mesh requirements.

interviewTip: Describe the Service Mesh advantage in microservice discovery: 'In modern Kubernetes environments, we use a Service Mesh like Istio with Envoy sidecars. The application code makes standard HTTP calls to service hostnames, while the local Envoy sidecar intercepts traffic, queries the discovery control plane, enforces mTLS encryption, and balances requests across healthy pods.'
